items.stem: A Webflow user creates a brand-new class for every single element and styling changes become unmanageable. What practice fixes this?

options.text: Reuse a shared class across similar elements so one change updates them all
options.rationale: Correct: reusing classes centralises styling and keeps a site maintainable.

options.text: Add inline styles to each element instead
options.rationale: Inline styles scatter rules and make maintenance worse.

options.text: Create one class per page regardless of element
options.rationale: Page-scoped single classes do not match elements to shared styles.

options.text: Avoid classes and style the body only
options.rationale: Styling only the body cannot target individual components.

items.explanation: Correct: reusing classes centralises styling and keeps a site maintainable.

items.stem: Which TWO tasks should be completed before publishing a Webflow site so it is findable and functional? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Setting page titles and meta descriptions for SEO
options.rationale: Correct: page-level SEO settings help the site be found and described correctly.

options.text: Verifying the contact form submits and routes correctly
options.rationale: Correct: a broken form means lost leads, so it must be tested before launch.

options.text: Choosing a different logo animation style
options.rationale: Logo animation is cosmetic and not a launch prerequisite.
Internal labels are organisational and do not affect the published site.

items.explanation: Correct: page-level SEO settings help the site be found and described correctly.

items.stem: A three-column layout looks right on desktop but columns are squashed and unreadable on phones. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Adjust the layout at the smaller breakpoints so the columns stack or resize for mobile
options.rationale: Correct: responsive layouts must be tuned per breakpoint, typically stacking columns on narrow screens.
You cannot rely on users to compensate for a broken layout.

options.text: Remove two of the columns permanently
options.rationale: Deleting content is unnecessary; the layout just needs responsive settings.

options.text: Set a fixed pixel width for the page
options.rationale: A fixed width prevents the page from adapting to phone screens.

items.explanation: Correct: responsive layouts must be tuned per breakpoint, typically stacking columns on narrow screens.
